German: das
English: who / which (neuter nominative)

German: Das Kind, das weint, ist müde.
English: The child who is crying is tired.

German: dem
English: to whom / to which (dative masculine/neuter)

German: Der Mann, dem ich helfe, ist alt.
English: The man whom I am helping is old.

German: den
English: whom / which (masculine accusative)

German: Der Hund, den du siehst, ist groß.
English: The dog that you see is big.

German: der
English: who / which (masculine nominative)

German: Der Mann, der dort steht, ist mein Bruder.
English: The man who is standing there is my brother.

German: deren
English: whose / of which (feminine/plural genitive)

German: Die Frau, deren Auto kaputt ist, wartet.
English: The woman whose car is broken is waiting.

German: dessen
English: whose / of which (masculine/neuter genitive)

German: Der Mann, dessen Sohn krank ist, arbeitet.
English: The man whose son is sick is working.

German: die
English: who / which (feminine nominative / plural)

German: Die Frau, die ich meine, ist klug.
English: The woman whom I mean is smart.

German: welche
English: which (feminine/plural nominative)

German: Die Blume, welche rot ist, riecht gut.
English: The flower which is red smells good.

German: welchem
English: to which (dative masculine/neuter)

German: Der Freund, welchem ich vertraue, hilft mir.
English: The friend whom I trust helps me.

German: welchen
English: which (masculine accusative)

German: Den Film, welchen ich sah, mag ich.
English: The movie which I saw, I like.

German: welcher
English: which (masculine nominative - formal)

German: Der Stuhl, welcher hier steht, ist alt.
English: The chair which stands here is old.

German: welches
English: which (neuter nominative)

German: Das Buch, welches ich lese, ist spannend.
English: The book which I am reading is exciting.
